blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fenofibrate and severe hypertriglyceridemia
stem: An adult with persistent severe hypertriglyceridemia (fasting triglycerides 620 mg/dL) is prescribed fenofibrate after secondary causes and lifestyle measures are addressed. Which therapeutic effect should the nurse expect?

options.A: A clinically meaningful reduction in triglyceride-rich lipoproteins; fenofibrate is indicated to lower triglycerides in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia.
options.B: A primary antihypertensive effect with little expected change in triglycerides because fenofibrate acts mainly by reducing systemic vascular resistance.
options.C: Selective LDL-C lowering with minimal triglyceride effect because fenofibrate acts primarily through intestinal cholesterol-absorption inhibition.
options.D: Reliable elimination of pancreatitis risk once triglycerides begin to fall because fenofibrate treatment has been shown to guarantee prevention of acute pancreatitis.

rationale: Current fenofibrate labeling indicates the drug as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia, defined in the label as TG at least 500 mg/dL. The 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline identifies fibric acid derivatives as triglyceride-lowering medications and notes typical TG reductions of about 30% to 50%. The label separately states that although markedly elevated triglycerides can increase pancreatitis risk, the effect of fenofibrate therapy on reducing that risk has not been determined. Therefore A is correct. B and C misstate the therapeutic effect, and D overstates the evidence.
educational_objective: Recognize fenofibrate as a triglyceride-lowering option for adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia while avoiding the unsupported claim that treatment guarantees prevention of pancreatitis.
source_organization: DailyMed / FDA labeling; American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association and partner societies
source_document_title: FENOFIBRATE — Full Prescribing Information; 2026 ACC/AHA Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia
source_version_date: Current fenofibrate DailyMed labeling published in 2026; 2026 dyslipidemia guideline published March 13, 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Fenofibrate Indications and Usage: adjunct to diet to reduce TG in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia (TG ≥500 mg/dL); limitation states effect on reducing pancreatitis risk has not been determined. 2026 guideline §4.2.1.3 and severe hypertriglyceridemia supportive text: fibric acid derivatives lower TG about 30%-50% and are among TG-lowering options for severe hypertriglyceridemia.
source_claim_supported: Fenofibrate is indicated to lower triglycerides in severe hypertriglyceridemia and typically produces substantial TG reduction; it should not be described as guaranteeing prevention of pancreatitis.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate therapeutic medication effects; monitor response; provide safe medication education.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete therapeutic-effect statements of comparable length.
Removed the original key-length cue and tightened the evidence wording so pancreatitis prevention is not presented as guaranteed.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely describes the expected fenofibrate therapeutic effect without overstating pancreatitis prevention. Options are tightly length-matched.
